reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a $3,500 package as producing 1,150 Clubcoins and an asserted immediate $718 benefit, alongside claimed daily passive income and team-based commissions. The package discussion includes invitations and a supplied referral link, presenting a payment-to-benefit and recruitment-related flow. The review framing and account disclaimer provide context, but the stated package terms, payouts, and external claims are not verified.

citations.quote: in about one year I bought the largest pool for $,500 dollars now I have 3 pools working
all these 3 pools bring me passive income a day
if you go to the package three and a half thousand dollars then you get a present 1150
gift from the company for registering for $3,5k

opening.argument: Judge the figures as an account of past results and a calculation, not a promise to viewers. The account screen cautions that its USD values are approximate and depend on the exchange rate when commissions or invoices were earned or paid. The speaker also makes the bitcoin-to-dollar conversion conditional on the day's rate. Those qualifications matter: neither an approximate historical display nor a rate-dependent calculation establishes what a new participant will receive.

citations.quote: let's count how much it will be dollars if by today's rate for one bitcoin $ 666

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a package, a gift calculation and daily income, but it treats different kinds of figures as one promised return. The speaker calls the daily income his own experience with three pools, while the account screen says USD figures are approximate. A personal history and an approximate valuation do not establish a guaranteed result for the judge's hypothetical new buyer.

citations.quote: now I have 3 pools working you see them on the screen 1 2 pool 3 all these 3 pools bring me passive income a day

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An exchange-rate disclaimer limits the precision of displayed USD equivalents; it does not qualify the pitch for buying a package. The speaker says three purchased pools bring him daily passive income and tells viewers that registering for the $3,500 package brings a gift. Whether those claims are guaranteed or verified is beside the central point: payment is being promoted through claimed benefits and recurring returns.

citations.quote: all these 3 pools bring me passive income a day
gift from the company for registering for $3,5k

opening.argument: This is presented as a review and a walk-through of an account, not merely an instruction to purchase. The speaker says he will show his results, then explains how to locate a date and total income in the displayed records. He also points viewers to an outside resource where they can inspect mining information. A demonstration of what an account reports and where to check a claim can be evaluated as such without treating the reported results as verified or repeatable.

citations.quote: Bitclub Network REVIEWS Bitclub Network
Now I would like to show you my results.
In this column you could see your total income.
you can look at this information on the blockchain's independent resource through the blockchain.info link.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The package and income passages are real, but the opening leaves out how much of the presentation is spent walking through dated account entries and showing where a total appears. A referral link establishes that the speaker may benefit from interest; it does not, by itself, turn every account demonstration into a claim that viewers will achieve the same results. The displayed history remains a demonstration of reported entries, not proof of future payouts.

citations.quote: let's take this page and take the day of November 18, 2014 you can see the date in this column
In this column you could see your total income.
Bitclub Network Referral Link: http://bitclub.network/nbuksanova

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walk-through can still be a sales pitch. The speaker pairs the account demonstration with claims that purchased pools generate daily passive income, and the description supplies a referral link. He then addresses prospective buyers directly with a $3,500 package benefit and his own additional payment. The account entries do not verify those benefits, while their use in this presentation supports the promotional reading.

citations.quote: all these 3 pools bring me passive income a day
Bitclub Network Referral Link: http://bitclub.network/nbuksanova
Those who buy a 3,5k package I personally give but only in dollars!

opening.argument: The concrete viewer-facing offer can be read as a referral promotion: the speaker describes Clubcoins as a company gift tied to a package and says he personally adds a payment for buyers. That is different from establishing that the gift is a guaranteed cash withdrawal or that buyers must recruit others to receive it. He even describes his existing team as investors who do not build networks. The evidence shows a promoted purchase and an incentive, but it does not spell out a required downline or demonstrate what a new buyer can redeem.

citations.quote: 1150 Clubcoins by 32 cents means $368 in gift from the company for registering for $3,5k
Those who buy a 3,5k package I personally give but only in dollars!
They are all investors, and none of them does anything, they do not build networks

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening combines package pricing, passive income and team activity into a single recruitment mechanism. Yet the speaker says the team members do not build networks, and describes the extra buyer payment as something he personally gives. The cited package language supports a purchase incentive; it does not establish that a buyer must assemble a team, or that the stated Clubcoin valuation is immediately redeemable cash.

citations.quote: They are all investors, and none of them does anything, they do not build networks
I give myself 10% of this amount, those who buy free gift on $3 500, which equal 350 dollars.
1150 Clubcoins by 32 cents means $368 in gift from the company for registering for $3,5k

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A mandatory downline is not necessary to recognize this offer's payment-to-return pitch. The speaker links bought pools to daily passive income, describes commissions from team members in the displayed account, and says a $3,500 buyer can get $718 back instantly. Calling part of that sum a gift does not remove the asserted immediate benefit, and the supplied material does not verify that it is redeemable.
